question: Master account, limited account or payment account: what is the difference?
answer: A master account gives full access to the Fed's payment services and its credit. A limited-purpose account (so far only Kraken's) gives payment access without the Fed's credit, and the proposed payment account would do something similar for a new class of firms. Without any account, a firm reaches the Fed only through a bank that has one.

sections.title: Side by side
sections.sub: Each cell says what the account allows, with the reason underneath. On a phone, swipe the table sideways.

rows.text: Institutions that are legally eligible under the Federal Reserve Act (mainly depository institutions and member banks), at the Reserve Bank's discretion. The Board's 2022 guidelines sort requests into three tiers: Tier 1 = federally insured institutions (lightest review); Tier 2 = not federally insured but supervised by a federal banking agency, with any holding company under Fed oversight; Tier 3 = not federally insured and not federally supervised at the bank or holding-company level (strictest review). Two appeals courts (Tenth Circuit in Custodia, 2025; Second Circuit in Banco San Juan, 2026) held that eligibility does not create a right to an account, and an account can be taken away.

rows.note: Full access to Reserve Bank services such as Fedwire Funds, Fedwire Securities, FedACH, FedNow, the National Settlement Service and cash services, subject to each service's terms.
Eligible institutions earn interest on reserve balances.
Depository institutions can borrow from the discount window if they meet its credit and collateral rules.
Daytime overdrafts are allowed within caps under the Fed's Payment System Risk policy.

Federal Reserve Act (Reserve Banks 'may' receive deposits, 12 U.S.C. 342; Monetary Control Act pricing and access, 12 U.S.C. 248a); Board Guidelines for Evaluating Account and Services Requests (Aug 15, 2022); Reserve Bank Operating Circular 1. Buying Federal Reserve Bank stock (membership), which the OCC requires of new national trust banks, is a separate step and does not by itself give an account.

rows: Limited-purpose ("skinny") account — Kraken Financial's one-off account

rows.text: One institution so far: Kraken Financial, approved by the Kansas City Fed on Mar 4, 2026 under existing law. The Kansas City Fed says this did not create a new account category or widen who is eligible; Fed Vice Chair Bowman called it a pilot for this one institution.

rows.note: Fedwire Funds only, with any payment that would overdraw the account rejected automatically. Kraken says no FedNow or ACH.
No interest on balances.
No discount-window credit.
No intraday credit; end-of-day balance is capped (amount not published).
Kansas City Fed's discretion under the Federal Reserve Act and the Board's 2022 Account Access Guidelines; one-year initial term.

rows.text: Any institution legally eligible for a Reserve Bank account, whatever its tier; an institution could not hold both a Payment Account and a master account. Reserve Banks would decide requests, generally within 90 days of a complete file. The proposal does not widen legal eligibility.

rows.note: Only services where overdrafts can be rejected automatically: Fedwire Funds, FedNow, the National Settlement Service, and Fedwire Securities transfers free of payment. No FedACH and no securities delivery-versus-payment.
No interest on balances (Regulation D proposal).
No discount-window credit (Regulation A proposal).
No intraday credit. End-of-day balance capped at a level set per institution, at most $1 billion; no limit on balances during the day.

Proposed new Part IV of the Fed's Payment System Risk policy and revised Account Access Guidelines (Docket OP-1878, Federal Register 2026-10375, 91 FR 30627), with amendments to Regulation D (2026-10377) and Regulation A (2026-10376). Board approved May 20, 2026; published May 26, 2026; comments closed July 27, 2026. The Board asked Reserve Banks to pause Tier 3 decisions until it finishes. Preceded by a Dec 23, 2025 request for information.

rows: No Fed account (using a correspondent bank)

rows.text: Any firm with a bank relationship. The firm's payments settle through another bank's Fed account (for example, Kraken customer wires still go through Dart Bank). The Fed's database lists institutions that settle through another depository institution's account as having access this way.

rows.note: Indirect only, on the correspondent bank's terms and hours.
None from the Fed directly; any interest comes from the correspondent bank.
None from the Fed directly.
None from the Fed directly; any credit is from the correspondent.
Private contract with the correspondent bank.

research.title: The Fed is many legal bodies, and its building cost doubled
research.answer: The Federal Reserve remains a congressionally created system of Board, FOMC and separately chartered Reserve Banks—not a literal fourth branch—but 2026 doctrine preserves exceptional cause protection for Governors.
